binders: A type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
hypotheses: S is measurable into the Borel measurable space on ℝ.
The function ω ↦ exp(λ·S(ω)) is integrable with respect to μ.
conclusions: The real-valued measure of the event {ω | S(ω) ≥ t} is at most exp(−λt) times the integral of exp(λ·S(ω)) with respect to μ.
mathematical_definitions: Set.Ici t is the interval [t,∞) = {x ∈ ℝ | t ≤ x}.
Set.preimage S (Set.Ici t) is the upper-tail event {ω ∈ Ω | S(ω) ≥ t}.
μ.real(A) is ENNReal.toReal applied to the measure μ(A).
The integral is the real-valued Bochner integral ∫ exp(λS) dμ.
Because μ is assumed to be a probability measure, the integral may be read as the exponential moment Eμ[exp(λS)] and μ.real of the event as its probability.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable real-valued random variable S on a probability space, every real threshold t, and every positive real λ, if exp(λS) is integrable, then Pμ(S ≥ t) ≤ exp(−λt) Eμ[exp(λS)].

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement applies only to measures carrying an IsProbabilityMeasure instance, even though the displayed inequality has a more general measure-theoretic form.
The parameter λ is restricted to be strictly positive.
The exponential transform exp(λS) must be integrable; cases with an infinite or otherwise nonintegrable exponential moment are excluded rather than assigned an extended-real right side.
The threshold t is unrestricted and may be any real number.
The target encodes only an upper-tail bound for the event S ≥ t; it asserts no lower-tail, two-sided, independence, centering, or moment-generating-function neighborhood condition.
The proposition is conditional, so for a particular S and λ it says nothing when the integrability hypothesis is unavailable.

The use of Measure.real would be hazardous for an infinite event measure because ENNReal.toReal maps infinity non-faithfully, but the probability-measure assumption makes all event measures finite under the standard meaning of that typeclass.
ambiguities: The one-level body of MeasureTheory.integral is opaque in the dossier, although its type identifies the standard real-valued Bochner integral.
The internal fields of the inductive IsProbabilityMeasure declaration are not displayed; interpreting it as normalization μ(Ω) = 1 relies on its standard library semantics.
